claim: The multi-modal instruction is formed by concatenating aligned modality representations (ha_i, ha_v, ha_a) with the embedding of the textual instruction tokens.
falsifier: One can verify that the multi-modal instruction x equals the concatenation of ha_i, ha_v, ha_a, and Embed(xt) as defined in the source.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Multi-modal instruction integration–multi-modal instruction…

claim: Matryoshka SAEs achieve comparable or better performance than standard SAE architectures when trained on protein language models.
falsifier: Train Matryoshka SAEs and standard SAEs on the same protein language model and compare performance on a held-out set of concepts and contact map prediction; the hypothesis predicts non-inferiority of Matryoshka SAEs.

conditions: Evaluation on biological concept discovery and contact map prediction
exclusions: Evidence is limited to ESM2 models, the specific Matryoshka implementation, and the evaluated tasks; transfer to other models or tasks is unestablished.

title: Matryoshka SAE architecture for Performance on concept discovery

claim: Switching energy in PECVD silicon nitride microring resonators is inversely proportional to the product of linear absorption coefficient, quality factor squared, and mode volume (α × Q²/V), and is minimized near the chemical bond absorption peak at 1520 nm.
falsifier: Fabricate PECVD SiN microring resonators with varying Q and V, measure switching energy at different wavelengths, and verify the inverse proportionality to α × Q²/V.

exclusions: limited to the reported PECVD system and experimental conditions

title: Linear absorption coefficient–switching energy principle
